title: 9 BOTTLES OF AUSTRALIAN WINE, ...
reason: Title says Australian wine but the nine bottles are mostly NZ, French and German, including a Patrick Piuze Chablis 2012, Shaw + Smith M3 2013, Cloudy Bay, a 1977 German Spaetlese and a 1975 Lions Club Tasmanian novelty; roughly $120 to $220 retail if sound.
findings: Title says Australian wine including Tasmanian, but the photos show a mixed lot where most bottles are from New Zealand, France and Germany. Nine bottles, labels read at full size and in crops: (1) 'Dr Van Diemen's Quite Amazing Tasmanian Devil Red Elixir', a purple-print novelty label with the Lions Club emblem and a comic cure-all list, dated 1975 and ending 'Convention ... November 1975' (partly legible), on a green bottle with a dark capsule; (2) Babich Black Label Sauvignon Blanc 2010, Marlborough, NZ; (3) Cloudy Bay Sauvignon Blanc (Marlborough, vintage not legible, screwcap); (4) Monowai Pinot Noir, Crownthorpe, Hawke's Bay, NZ (vintage reads 2016, last digit unclear); (5) Shaw + Smith M3 Chardonnay, Adelaide Hills, 2013; (6) Mildara 'Southern Cross' Late Harvest Muscat Blanc (older-style label, blue capsule, no vintage visible); (7) Dogrock (red dog logo) with a heavily foxed label that looks like Shiraz, vintage not legible; (8) a German 1977 Silvaner Qualitaetswein mit Praedikat Spaetlese, 'Herxheimer am Berg' (rest of the vineyard name torn off), 10.5% vol, eagle-crest label, gold foil capsule, wine deep amber; (9) Chablis, Terroir de Chichee, Vendanges 2012, Patrick Piuze, Chablis AC, product of France, cream closure, clean label. So only about four bottles (Shaw + Smith, Mildara, Dogrock and the Tasmanian novelty) are Australian. The Piuze Chablis, Shaw + Smith M3 and Cloudy Bay are the better-known names.
condition: Fill levels look normal in all nine (necks filled to or near the shoulder, none visibly low), though dark and coloured glass makes this hard to confirm. Capsules intact. Dr Van Diemen's label is stained and worn with brown spotting; Dogrock label is foxed and stained; the German label is torn at the left edge; the German wine and Shaw + Smith look deep gold to amber, so may be tired or oxidised. Others clean and dusty. Sold as is, storage history unknown.
rescore_note: Nine bottles, mostly NZ, French and German despite the title; Piuze Chablis 2012, Shaw + Smith M3 2013 and Cloudy Bay carry the value, but several whites look amber and storage is unknown; my estimate about $60 to $100 (no live comps).
